thread.title: Apple Stock In Holding Pattern Ahead Of Apple Earnings, Launch | Investor's Business Daily

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple Stock In Holding Pattern Ahead Of Apple Earnings, Launch | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Apple ( AAPL ) stock is trending sideways along its 50-day moving average ahead of two potential catalysts this week. The consumer electronics giant is holding a product launch event Tuesday. Apple earnings for its September quarter are due Thursday.
X Amid a broad market sell-off, Apple shares dropped 1.9% to close at 212.24 on the stock market today . Apple stock has been trading in a tight range for the past two weeks. It notched a record high of 233.47 on Oct. 3 before the recent tech stock sell-off.
The Cupertino, Calif.-based company is holding a product launch event Tuesday in New York City . Analysts expect Apple to introduce new iPad Pro tablets and Mac computers at the event, which starts at 10 a.m. local time.
The new iPad Pro models are rumored to mirror the design of the latest iPhones. They are expected to scrap the physical home button and use facial-recognition technology for unlocking the device. Apple also is likely to trot out a new Apple Pencil stylus at the event.

Apple Earnings Seen Rising 34% After the market close on Thursday, Apple earnings for its fiscal fourth quarter ended Sept. 29 are due. Analysts expect Apple to earn $2.78 a share, up 34% year over year, on sales of $61.59 billion, up 17%.
Apple earnings will include just nine days of sales of the company's 12th-generation smartphones, the iPhone XS and XS Max. A third model, the iPhone XR, went on sale Friday.
Analysts will be paying close attention to growth in Apple's services businesses, which include Apple Music, Apple Pay, iCloud and AppleCare.
For the December quarter, Wall Street is modeling Apple to earn $4.95 a share, up 27%, on sales of $93.01 billion, up 5%.
Services To Buoy Apple Stock: Analyst Jefferies analyst Timothy O'Shea on Monday reiterated his buy rating on Apple stock with a price target of 265.
"We believe Apple's stable iPhone business will serve as the foundation upon which it can build a massive, recurring and high-margin services business," O'Shea said in a report to clients. Services could account for 25% of the company's revenue and 40% of gross profit by fiscal 2022, he said.
Apple likely generated $38.8 billion in revenue from services in fiscal 2018, O'Shea said.
Services could lift the valuation of Apple stock, he said. Investors give higher multiples to services businesses than they do to lower-margin hardware businesses, he said.
